A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey-based research work. All 13 pages of each version, including six figures, Table 1, the appendix questionnaire, and the language list, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original survey results from 81 respondents, including quantitative distributions and qualitative analysis of language-resource practices and credit attribution.

after.justification: v5 retains the original 81-response survey results and adds several qualitative observations and respondent examples.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a computational algorithm or model. The survey-based approach is retained; terminology changes concerning participatory frameworks do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same respondents, language-resource practices, and languages listed in Appendix A.2. New language examples in Section 3.2 explain classification ambiguity rather than expand the surveyed population.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baseline systems or competing methods against a proposed method. Discussion of translation tools, LLMs, and annotation platforms does not constitute such evaluation.

E3.justification: The June–October 2024 recruitment period, recruitment channels, 81 responses, optional and multiple-choice questions, and manual qualitative processing are retained. Appendix A.1's questionnaire is unchanged; revised summaries do not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: Section 4.2.2 adds a qualitative comparison across project affiliations, stating that the discussed problems were equally observed in academia and industry. This modestly extends the thematic analysis, although no supporting subgroup counts or separate robustness tests are provided.

E5.justification: Both versions report descriptive counts and percentages without confidence intervals, significance tests, repeated-study information, or uncertainty estimates. The reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the numerical figure contents are unchanged. v5 adds the academia–industry observation in Section 4.2.2 and reports small company gifts for months of labor and work being used by more prominent individuals in Sections 4.3 and 5.1. These extend the qualitative findings from the retained survey.

T1.justification: Neither version contains formal mathematical definitions, theorems, derivations, or proofs. Changes to conceptual explanations do not introduce formal theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: documenting researchers' and data workers' experiences and recommending culturally appropriate, fair resource-development practices. The conclusion's novelty claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds legal-contract guidance, clarifies balancing community needs with research interests, and removes the reviewer-request qualification on proof of fair payment. Section 5.5 drops explicit translation-quality controls and per-language reporting advice, while Section 4.2.2 removes the blanket multilingual-versus-monolingual performance assertion. The paper's selection-bias limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The complete questionnaire, recruitment information, manual answer-processing description, and respondent confidentiality policy are retained. Moving respondent-language caveats to Appendix A.2 does not add reproducibility information; no new analysis implementation or study-data access instructions appear.

R1.justification: v5 adds Ramponi (2024), revises the description of Lent et al. (2022) to specify Creole respondents, and removes the footnote linking authorship guidelines. The broader positioning within community-centered NLP research remains stable.

P1.justification: v5 makes local wording and paragraph revisions throughout, particularly around participatory frameworks and recommendations, while retaining the narrative structure. A respondent caveat moves from Section 3.1 to Appendix A.2, and limitations and ethics headings become unnumbered. Some editing errors are introduced, including duplicated text.

P2.justification: All six figure images and Table 1's structure are retained. Figure 1's caption is reframed around stakeholders, several other captions receive small edits, and text reflow changes spacing and placement. There are no new or redrawn visualizations.

improvement.justification: v5 gains concreteness through participant examples and refined contract and community-engagement advice. However, it removes linked authorship standards and explicit per-language quality-control guidance, while introducing a misplaced Figure 3 reference in Section 5.2 and duplicated caption text in Section 4.2.2. With the quantitative evidence and questionnaire unchanged, these competing gains in explanation and losses in clarity and practical guidance do not establish a reliable net direction.
